fugues.name: The Canon
fugues.title: Fugue 1 in C major

sound.name: PIPE ORGAN
sound.why: Four voices in continuous stretti over pedal points (Ledbetter's last section, bars 19-27), the subject in long, vocal steps: the stile antico of the organ ricercar, which D246 already heard on the organ. The pedal's sustained C under the close carries on a phone through the organ's upper ranks.
sound.character: Quiet, austere (Keller); stretti from bar 7, triple and quadruple stretti 14-19, stretti over pedals 19-27 (Ledbetter); hardly any episode.

moments.why: The exposition on the flutes: Bodky's clavichord plan begins soft (bars 1-7).
The close stretto (Ledbetter 7-14): the principals, Bodky's crescendo made a terrace.
Triple and quadruple stretto after the cadence in A minor (14-19): the plenum, Bodky's loudest span.
The stretti over the pedal points (19-27) back on the principals: Bodky's diminuendo toward a soft close.

s1.name: 4' FLUTE
s1.why: Serene and slow, entries crowded in stretto: a soft sine an octave above haloes every note without a new accent, so overlapping entries stay calm.

fugues.stage: The Canon: the footlights warm; a cold spot from above; the whole stage lit.

fugues.name: The Imp
fugues.title: Fugue 2 in C minor

sound.name: ABBEY ROAD
sound.why: D523: 4/4 at a crotchet of 70, its subject a riff of semiquavers (Keller's capricious, half-jesting fugue) that a rock band's backbeat carries without a note changed: ABBEY ROAD, the Gretsch on the subject's top, the rock piano inside, the picked bass, the drums' fills into each entry and the break before the last entry (bar 29).
sound.character: Regular alternation of entries and episodes (Bodky); episodes 5-7, 9-11, 13-15, 17-20, 22-26; the bass entry at 26 after the dominant pedal; a forte close (Keller).

s1.name: GLASS SPARK
s1.why: Steady sixteenths, sharp: a short glassy FM-bell ping an octave up on the eighths only, the subject's skeleton, crisp as the subject, never on every sixteenth.

moments.why: the Soprano's answer in g (bar 3)
the Bass's subject in c (bar 7)
after the episode, the Soprano's subject in Eb (bar 11)
after the episode, the Alto's answer in g (bar 15)
after the episode, the Soprano's subject in c (bar 20)
after the episode, the Bass's subject in c (bar 26)
the break before the final entry, the Soprano's subject in c (bar 29)
the final chord: the closing flourish

fugues.stage: The Imp: the fire lower, embers; the cave's blue depths; the fire flaring up.

fugues.name: The Stone-Skipper
fugues.title: Fugue 3 in C♯ major

sound.name: GAME BOY
sound.why: Graceful, euphonious, not too brilliant (Keller), three voices with long chattering episodes: the Game Boy's thin pulses and wave channel keep the three lines apart through a phone's speaker, and its duty cycles give the episodes a colour of their own.
sound.character: A first section 1-12, long episodes (7-14, 28-34, 48-55), a reprise from 42 (Ledbetter); a proud close (Keller).

moments.why: The episode 7-10 (Ledbetter): the upper pulses thinner, a chattering colour.
The episode 7-10 (Ledbetter): the upper pulses thinner, a chattering colour.
The soprano's entry: the voices' own widths.
The long episode 28-34 thinner again.
The long episode 28-34 thinner again.
The entries of 35-36.
The reprise (Ledbetter 42-55): the lead's square, fuller.

s1.name: PIZZICATO 4'
s1.why: Seven sharps of joy, a skipping dance in quavers and semiquavers: a tiny triangle pluck an octave up on the quavers only lightens the skips.

fugues.stage: The Stone-Skipper: the golden hour; dusk on the pond; the sunset on the water.

fugues.name: The Cross
fugues.title: Fugue 4 in C♯ minor

sound.name: STRING CONSORT
sound.why: Five voices, three subjects, a ricercar in the stile antico (Bodky: 'monumental'): a viol consort's music, played by STRING CONSORT one to a part (two violins, two violas, cello), each line its own bow.
sound.character: Heavy first section, a more subjective second (the running second subject from 35), the highest inward intensity in the third (from 49; Keller); the stretto 94-115 (Ledbetter) over pedals on A♭ and C♯.

busoni.heading: Gravemente e sostenuto, ma non troppo.

s1.name: 16' PEDAL
s1.why: The solemn cross-motif in long notes: a soft octave below, an organ's 16', grounds it, in a larger room.

s2.name: SECOND CHOIR
s2.why: The running quavers: the voice doubled 7 cents off (a harpsichord's second 8' choir), thicker without new attacks.

s3.name: BELL
s3.why: The repeated-note figure: a small bell two octaves up on each note makes the repetitions ring.

fugues.stage: The Cross: night comes, the stars; the dark and the mist; dawn behind the cross.

fugues.name: The Coronation
fugues.title: Fugue 5 in D major

sound.name: BACH BRASS
sound.why: The Coronation: a French overture fugue, eroico, sempre f, its dotted rhythms and its pomp the trumpets in D of a festive cantata (Bodky's 'full work'): BACH BRASS, the trumpets on top, the tongued dots crisp, its bass tight on a phone.
sound.character: Dignified, strong, with fire (Keller); the right hand on the softer manual 6-8, 9-11, 21-22, the left 17-20 (Bodky).

busoni.heading: Allegro moderato ed eroico, piuttosto Andante.

moments.why: The overture's pomp: the trumpets in D, sempre f.
Bodky's softer right hand (6-8) as the upper brass a shade mellower.
The full choir again from the first chord of 8.
Bodky's softer left hand (17-20): the low brass mellower.
The close blazing, into more of the church.

s1.name: TRUMPET BITE
s1.why: A festive French overture: a brass blip at each attack sharpens the dotted runs like trumpets.

fugues.stage: The Coronation: the window's light in shafts; the banners' red; the window ablaze.

fugues.name: The Ambush
fugues.title: Fugue 6 in D minor

sound.name: JAZZ QUARTET
sound.why: D510: Bodky's clavichord fugue, its running semiquavers over 3/4 (the clavichord withdrawn): JAZZ QUARTET's waltz, the vibraphone on the subject, the piano inside, the plucked bass, Busoni's dolce and swells in the band's dynamics, the brushes in three.
sound.character: Stretti massing throughout; a first half 1-21 and a second half in inversion 21-44 (Ledbetter); episodes 9-13, 30-33.

s1.name: TRAVERSO
s1.why: A singing scale up to the B flat, then a sigh: a breathy flute an octave up on the longer notes carries the rise without touching the quick turn.

inverted.name: TRAVERSO BELOW
inverted.why: Upside down, its flute turned over too: the same breath an octave below, so the mirrored entries are heard as mirrors.

brushes.why: the climax: the final entries
the final cadence's approach
the final chord: a soft flutter, fading

fugues.stage: The Ambush: dusk and mist in the trees; night and rain; the moon rising over the road.

fugues.name: The Bicycle
fugues.title: Fugue 7 in E♭ major

sound.name: SWITCHED-ON
sound.why: Wendy Carlos recorded this prelude and fugue on Switched-On Bach (1968): the Moog's lines are clear and dry on a phone, the bass a snapping synth bass.
sound.character: Charming, free and modern (Keller); an elegant 'secular' fugue, first half 1-17 (Ledbetter), episodes three quarters of it.

moments.why: The second half (17-25) with the filter half closed, Bodky's softer span.
Open again from 25.
The last bars a shade brighter (Bodky's coupled close).

s1.name: POSTHORN
s1.why: Bold and light in E flat, the horn's key, ending in a broken chord: a horn blip on the head and a small bell on each leap of the arpeggio.

fugues.stage: The Bicycle: the noon heat; the late afternoon; the sun at the road's end.

fugues.name: The Pilgrim
fugues.title: Fugue 8 in D♯ minor

sound.name: PIANO (SAMPLED)
sound.why: Spiritually intense, searching (Keller), with inner, not outward grandeur (Bodky, a clavichord piece): a singing piano holds its long lines and augmentations; its bass is clear on a phone.
sound.character: Six expositions, to be set off as units (Keller: mp, mf, p, mf, f): 1-19, 19-30, 30-52 (inversion), 52-62, 62-77 (augmentation), 77-87.

moments.why: Keller's mp for the first exposition: the soft layer.
The second exposition (mf) after the cadence in A♯ minor.
The inversion (Keller's p).
The stretto of 52 (mf).

s1.name: NAZARD
s1.why: Learned and slow: a faint twelfth above (an organ's 2 2/3' mutation) colours the subject as written.

inverted.name: MIRROR 16'
inverted.why: The subject inverted, its colour mirrored too: the soft layer an octave below instead of above.

augmented.name: SLOW GIANT
augmented.why: The subject in augmentation: an octave above and below at once, an organ plenum, in the largest room.

fugues.stage: The Pilgrim: evening; night, the stars; the shrine's light at the road's end.

fugues.name: The Sparrow
fugues.title: Fugue 9 in E major

sound.name: BAROQUE BAND
sound.why: Cheeky and high-spirited (Keller), three voices like a trio sonata: BAROQUE BAND's violin and oboe, and the bass entering last (bar 4) on the cello with the continuo harpsichord.
sound.character: Vocal in idiom (Bodky); a long episode 10-16, a reprise from 19 (Ledbetter).

s1.name: 2' FLAUTINO
s1.why: Two notes and away, bright E major running on: the faintest sine two octaves up on the head and the longer notes, light as the run.

fugues.stage: The Sparrow: the clouds gathering; a shower over the roofs; the sun breaking through.

fugues.name: The Two Horsemen
fugues.title: Fugue 10 in E minor

sound.name: SOLO VOICES
sound.why: D510: the only two-voice fugue, its lines singing in long arcs and meeting in octaves (19, 38): SOLO VOICES' recorded soprano and bass, two distinct voices that blend (measured: within 1.4 dB of each other on a computer, 0.4 on a phone; the most even of four pairs tried).
sound.character: Two halves, the second a mirror of the first (Ledbetter 1-19, 20-38); the famous unisons in 19 and 38.

s1.name: TOCCATA ECHO
s1.why: Fast toccata runs in two voices: a short slapback echo on the other side, on the head and the longer notes (not every sixteenth), widens the line without blurring the runs.

fugues.stage: The Two Horsemen: the full day, dust; a dust storm; the sun high over the plain.

fugues.name: The Shepherdess
fugues.title: Fugue 11 in F major

sound.name: TOMITA
sound.why: A passepied, pastoral (Bodky, Keller: 'with deliberate grace'): TOMITA's synthesized flutes and whistles over its bass, a shepherd's dance in the space echo, the outer voices nearly dry for a phone.
sound.character: Bodky's three terraces (1-17, 17-34, 35-46, 46-56, 56-72); first section 1-46, stretto 46-56 (Ledbetter).

s1.name: LEAP SPARK
s1.why: A quick 3/8 dance of leaps: a short pluck an octave up on the head and on each note reached by a leap marks its springs.

fugues.stage: The Shepherdess: midday; an afternoon shower; the light after the rain.

fugues.name: The Requiem
fugues.title: Fugue 12 in F minor

sound.name: VOCAL SYNTH
sound.why: D510 (the owner: "I tested vocal synth and prefer it"): the anguished chromatic subject that 'must sing' (Bodky, Keller): VOCAL SYNTH's four singers sustain it in the plate, the calm interludes a shade darker.
sound.character: The chromatic entries against calm diatonic interludes (10-13, 16-18, 22-26, 50-52: Ledbetter), the contrast to be underlined (Keller).

busoni.heading: Molto sostenuto, ma fermo in tempo e carattere.

moments.why: The interlude 10-13 darker, against the chromatic subject (Keller).
The soprano's entry.
The interlude 22-26.
The bass's entry.
The interlude 50-52.
The last entry.

s1.name: REGAL 16'
s1.why: Ten chromatic steps in slow crotchets, severe: a dark reed an octave below gives each semitone weight, in a large room.

fugues.stage: The Requiem: the dark nave; moonlight through the windows; the vaults, incense in the air; dawn through the rose window.

fugues.name: The Aquarium
fugues.title: Fugue 13 in F♯ major

sound.name: ZELENKA TRIO
sound.why: Euphonious, soft and gently flowing (Keller), the 'little brook' of water figures (Bodky): D504's ZELENKA TRIO, two oboes of different breath in conversation and the bassoon, the continuo at the bass's entries, the cadences and the close.
sound.character: Exposition 1-7, then 7-23 and 23-35 (Ledbetter); episodes 7-11, 12-15, 17-20, 22-28.

continuo.why: The subject enters in the bass (5), closing the exposition: the continuo with it, under the two oboes' entries (1, 3).
The first episode (7-11), its water figures light: the reeds alone after the cadence in F# (7).
The approach to the perfect cadence in C# (11) and the soprano's return (11).
The episode 12-15 and the alto's entry (15): the oboes' conversation over the bassoon alone.
Toward the perfect cadence in C# (17).
The episode 17-20, light again.
The bass's entry in D# minor (20) and the cadences in D# minor (22, 23): the fugue's darkest moment.
The long episode (23-28) and the alto's B major entry (28): the reeds alone.
The last entry, the soprano's in F# (31), and the close (34-35) over the full continuo.

s1.name: CELESTA
s1.why: A sweet, robust theme in F sharp major with a turn: a celesta two octaves up on its longer notes, a glint over the warmth.

fugues.stage: The Aquarium: deeper, plankton drifting; the light from the surface in shafts; the sun on the water above.

fugues.name: Pierrot
fugues.title: Fugue 14 in F♯ minor

sound.name: JAZZ QUARTET
sound.why: D510 (the owner's choice: JAZZ QUARTET): pensive, a sobbing countersubject in 6/4 (Keller, Bodky): the vibraphone's held notes and the plucked bass in two beats a bar, the brushes soft.
sound.character: An episode 11-14 (Ledbetter), the cadence in C♯ minor (20) and the inversion's entry, a bass pedal on C♯ 37-39.

busoni.heading: Sostenuto e severo, ma piuttosto Andante.

s1.name: GAMBA
s1.why: A calm stepwise line in 6/4, long notes and suspensions: the voice doubled a few cents flat, a viol's slow beating, sustains the yearning.

brushes.why: the climax: the final entries
the final cadence's approach
the final chord: a soft flutter, fading

fugues.stage: Pierrot: the moon brighter, the stars; clouds over it; the moon full.

fugues.name: The Pinball
fugues.title: Fugue 15 in G major

sound.name: MEGA FM
sound.why: A gigue, 'a performer's fugue' of fire and humour with sharp articulation (Keller): MEGA FM's clav and slap bass articulate it crisply and cut through a phone's speaker.
sound.character: Bodky's three spans (1-37 forte, 38-61 piano, 61-86 forte); the exposition inverso 20-31 (Ledbetter); the final stretti 77-79.

moments.why: Bodky's middle span (38-61) with a mellower FM index.
The operators' own brightness from 61⅝ (Bodky).
The last stretti a little brighter.

s1.name: FIFE
s1.why: A long 6/8 gigue theme with leaps of a seventh: a thin fife ping an octave up on the quavers, the dance's piping.

inverted.name: ANSWERING ECHO
inverted.why: The entries stand on their heads: the inversion answered by a slapback on the other side, a reply rather than a pipe.

fugues.stage: The Pinball: the neon turns magenta; blue, sparks; the jackpot's glow.

fugues.name: The Knight
fugues.title: Fugue 16 in G minor

sound.name: ABBEY ROAD
sound.why: D523: four voices in 4/4 at a crotchet of 58, molto energico (Bodky), its dotted subject a heavy late-Beatles stride: ABBEY ROAD's two guitars, rock piano and picked bass one to a voice, the sixteenth hi-hat under the slow beat, Bodky's echo episode the drums' quieter cross-stick.
sound.character: Cadences in G minor (10) and B♭ (12); the echo of 18-20; the episode after the cadence of 24; stretto 28 (Bodky).

s1.name: TWELFTH BELL
s1.why: A short G minor subject that leans on its held F sharp: a soft bell a twelfth up on the longer notes rings the leading note and its resolution.

moments.why: the Soprano's answer in d (bar 2)
the Bass's subject in g (bar 5)
the Tenor's answer in d (bar 6), in stretto: a crash only

the Bass's subject in Bb (bar 17)
the Alto's subject in Eb (bar 17), in stretto: a crash only
the Bass's subject in c (bar 20)
the Soprano's subject in c (bar 21), in stretto: a crash only
the Alto's subject in g (bar 23)
after the episode, the Soprano's subject in g (bar 28)
the Tenor's subject in g (bar 28), in stretto: a crash only
the Bass's subject in g (bar 29), in stretto: a crash only
the Alto's subject in g (bar 31)
the break before the final entry, the Tenor's subject in g (bar 33)
the final chord: the closing flourish

fugues.stage: The Knight: candlelight on the board; the cold of the endgame; the mate's light.

fugues.name: The Diary
fugues.title: Fugue 17 in A♭ major

sound.name: PET SOUNDS
sound.why: 'Noble and warm … solemnly slow' (Keller): A flat major in 4/4 at a crotchet of 54, a 1966 ballad's tempo, four voices for a Pet Sounds session (the strings, the horn, the piano, the electric bass) over a soft backbeat with tambourine and the timpani's rhythm; the reprise (Ledbetter 27-35) out of a bar's break.
sound.character: A solo at 8-9 and episodes 11-12, 14-15, 19-20 (Ledbetter), a cadence in E♭ (23), the reprise 27-35.

s1.name: ARPEGGIO CHIME
s1.why: Seven notes opening on a falling A flat arpeggio: a glassy chime an octave up on each leap rings the chord and leaves the steps plain.

fugues.stage: The Diary: the afternoon sun; evening rain at the window; the sunset through it.

fugues.name: The Sleepwalker
fugues.title: Fugue 18 in G♯ minor

sound.name: PIANO (SAMPLED)
sound.why: Expressive but graceful, a free, almost romantic subject (Keller), a clavichord fugue for Bodky: the recorded grand, its four voices voiced apart (the inner ones lighter).
sound.character: Exposition 1-9 (Ledbetter); Bodky's idea: the exposition on the soft keyboard, the loud one from 11 to the end.

busoni.heading: Andante (non troppo) con un certo sentimento severo.

moments.why: Bodky's soft exposition: the soft layer.
From 11 the full tone (Bodky: 'we have to stay on it to the end').

s1.name: VOX HUMANA
s1.why: A sober, sighing subject in G sharp minor: a quiet reed in unison, the organ's voice stop, sings it.

fugues.stage: The Sleepwalker: mist over the roofs; the deep night, stars; dawn on the roofs.

fugues.name: The Three Stooges
fugues.title: Fugue 19 in A major

sound.name: JAZZ QUARTET

continuo.why: The subject opens in the bass (1): the continuo states the ground the trio's entries build on.
The answer in the tenor (5) and the upper entries (10, 14): the voices alone over the cello.
The bass's entry in G# minor (19), closing the exposition: the tension toward the cadence in F# (27).
The second subject enters (27-28): new matter, over the cello alone.
The bass's entries in E and C# minor (31, 36) about the cadence in B (35): the subjects combined.
An interlude of the upper voices (40-48).
The bass's G# minor entry in stretto with the soprano's C# minor (48-49), the bass in C# minor (54): the climax, to the cadences in E (59-61).
The long episode (61-75), the bass silent: the oboes and the bassoon alone.
The bass's return in B (75) after its long silence, and the cadence in G# minor (76).
The middle voices' entries (85, 86) over the cello alone.
The final group: the bass's G# and F# entries (89, 91), the soprano's last B (93), the pedal on E (94-95), the close in B (104).
